strings: Abercrombie appears to be a feeble, eccentric hermit dwelling in a dilapidated shack in western Duskwood near Raven Hill Cemetery. Claiming to be a harmless recluse plagued by the horrors of the woods, he readily enlists sympathetic travelers to gather peculiar reagents and supplies on his behalf.

Tucked away in the rotting shadows near Raven Hill Cemetery, Abercrombie cuts a pathetic figure. He presents himself as an old man merely trying to survive the terrors of Duskwood, asking travelers to run modest errands into Darkshire for supplies, herbs, and thread. To those unfamiliar with the history of the region, he seems like just another unfortunate soul left behind as the province fell into decay.

Before grief consumed his mind, Abercrombie was a respected, kindly alchemist living in Raven Hill. When his beloved wife, Eliza, died, sorrow broke his sanity. Turning to forbidden necromantic arts, he cut out his own heart and placed it within Eliza's dead breast to bring her back. The ritual succeeded only in creating a monster: Eliza returned cursed with an insatiable hunger for living flesh, forcing the mad alchemist to keep her buried in the cemetery.

Known in dark folklore simply as 'The Embalmer,' Abercrombie nurses a deep, psychotic grudge against the township of Darkshire and its leaders. The seemingly innocuous tasks he assigns to helpful adventurers—fetching ghoul ribs, specialty thread, and caustic brews—are actually the final components required to assemble Stitches, a colossal, flesh-stitched abomination engineered to slaughter the Night Watch and burn the town.

Aelthalyste is a banshee priest trainer and prominent figure within the Cult of Forgotten Shadows, stationed in the War Quarter of the Undercity. She oversees the spiritual discipline of Forsaken acolytes, teaching them to wield the dark energies of Shadow. She also coordinates with other Horde faith leaders, directing troll acolytes to their own elders in Orgrimmar.

Unlike many priests across Azeroth who revere the Holy Light, Aelthalyste guides the Forsaken through the tenets of the Cult of Forgotten Shadows. Rising as an incorporeal banshee, she embodies the spectral agony and relentless resolve of Sylvanas Windrunner's followers. From her chamber in the Undercity's War Quarter, she calls aspiring priests back from distant outposts to master the darker arts of their discipline, teaching them to harness suffering as a lethal weapon.

While her focus remains firmly on her Forsaken flock, Aelthalyste maintains mutual respect with other Horde spiritual practitioners. Recognizing the distinct nature of Darkspear spiritualism, she directs troll initiates away from her own shadow doctrines and sends them across the sea to Ur'kyo in Orgrimmar. This gesture of deference ensures that Horde spellcasters develop within their cultural traditions while cementing alliances between Kalimdor and Lordaeron.

Agathelos the Raging is a colossal armored boar penned within the thorned tunnels of Razorfen Kraul. Reared by the Death's Head quilboar as a living siege engine and avatar of their ancient god, he has been driven into a violent, unnatural frenzy. His sheer mass and strength make him one of the most dangerous beasts lurking under the southern Barrens.

Quilboar venerate all swine as descendants of their patron deity and progenitor, the god Agamaggan. To them, boars of exceptional size and tenacity are considered direct blessings from their fallen god. A beast the size of Agathelos—standing roughly twice as tall as a Barrens thunder lizard—carries massive spiritual and ceremonial significance among the Razorfen tribes.
A Weapon of the Death's Head

The Death's Head tribe, not content to leave Agathelos as merely a sacred icon, actively transformed him into a weapon of war. By force-feeding him the noxious bat guano gathered from the cavern ceilings of the Kraul, his handlers induced a maddened, unending delirium. The foul mixture drastically increased the colossal beast's stamina and fury, transforming him into a rampage waiting to be unleashed upon the tribe's rivals.

Because Agathelos is completely out of his mind with rage, even his handlers cannot let him roam loose within the Kraul. He is kept trapped in a dead-end tunnel behind an energetic ward maintained by quilboar shamans and guards. Should intruders break past the barrier, they face a beast driven completely wild by chemical madness, growing even more terrifying in size and power when struck.

Agathelos is naturally a massive specimen of swine, which the quilboar revere as a divine blessing of Agamaggan. His unnatural bulk and swollen strength were further enhanced by the Death's Head tribe feeding him potent bat guano to induce a hulking, berserk state.

Aku'mai is a monstrous, three-headed hydra dwelling in the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps along the Zoram Strand. Imbued with primordial shadow and favored by the ancient Old Gods, the beast is revered as a herald of apocalyptic ruin. The Twilight's Hammer cult tends to the creature in its submerged lair, offering living sacrifices to sate its eternal hunger.

Long before cultists claimed the sunken temple beneath the sea, Aku'mai haunted the coast of Ashenvale as a living blight upon the Zoram Strand. A creature of deep water and darker powers, this gargantuan hydra carries a fragment of the Old Gods' ancient malevolence within its three ravenous heads. Rather than an ordinary denizen of the tides, Aku'mai is an ancient terror that has lurked in the submerged ruins since the fall of the night elves' temple to Elune, poisoning the waters with Void-tainted malice.

Aku'mai's foul aura eventually drew the Twilight's Hammer deep into the subterranean caverns. Viewing the hydra as an anointed pet and harbinger of their dread masters, the cult established their sanctum around its nesting ground. Twilight Lord Kelris became consumed by the creature, convinced that tending to Aku'mai and facilitating its unending appetite would usher in the resurgence of the Old Gods and grant him eternal life. Cultists and captured captives alike are regularly cast into the hydra's pool to nourish its vile growth.

While VanCleef and the surviving masons fled into Westfall to form the Defias Brotherhood, Thredd was cast into the depths of the Stormwind Stockade.

For years, Thredd remained silent and seemingly forsaken behind iron bars. That isolation shattered with a massive prison riot that overran the guards, opening the cells and turning the Stockade into an armed fortress right under the Mage Quarter. Taking leadership of the imprisoned Defias bandits, insurgents, and allied cutthroats, Thredd established his command post in the eastern wing under the guard of an ogre named Hamhock.
